data.note:
Reflection on s_2e30d0950a (MG-132):

My conclusion Microtubule stabilizers (p0.48-0.62) was incorrect; true annotation is Protein degradation (BBBC021, PubChem CID 462382 identity confirmed, ChEMBL CHEMBL64925 no curated mechanism).

The error was over-weighting a single 39-cell well at 3uM (tub_mean z +54.7, tub_glcm_contrast z +151.7, cell_solidity +30.5) with microscopist description of diffuse bright tubulin and rounding, while the atlas was tied: per-well 4-way split (Protein degradation, Microtubule destabilizers, Microtubule stabilizers, Actin disruptors) and k=10 neighbours 5 stabilizer vs 4 destabilizer at effectively identical mean similarity 0.368. I discounted the 0.3-1uM phenotype (enlarged nuclei, stellate elongation, frac_large_nucleus z 15.3, nuc_major_axis z 13.6, act_std z 14.9) which is more consistent with proteasome-induced G2/M arrest and protein accumulation than taxane bundling.

MG-132 is a canonical peptide aldehyde proteasome inhibitor (Z-Leu-Leu-Leu-al). Literature returned confirms proteasome-mediated degradation in MCF-7 breast cancer cells (PMID 11562742) and toxicity of MG-132 via NF-kB inhibition (PMID 24992982), consistent with Protein degradation MoA. Proteasome inhibition stabilizes mitotic regulators (cyclins, aurora kinases, microtubule-associated proteins) and can produce secondary tubulin hyper-intensity/mitotic rounding that mimics stabilizers - explaining why the phenotype was ambiguous in composites.

Lesson: with a tied atlas and n=1 decisive well, probability should have remained at ~0.3-0.35 for each microtubule class and Protein degradation, with explicit budget caveat. Requested 3uM replicate 2 was appropriate but budget was exhausted; in a real lab I would repeat 3uM + 1uM, add phospho-H3 and ubiquitin accumulation assay vs reference proteasome inhibitor and stabilizer to disambiguate.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: Protein degradation (MG-132). My final submitted call: Microtubule stabilizers p=0.48, previously p=0.62. Verdict: incorrect.

What the evidence got right:
- The quantitative image features were dominated by a strong tubulin signal at the intermediate dose. Well w_b7bdfca819 (dose 4, 3uM, rep1) in e5 showed tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.7 and tub_mean z=+54.7 with cell_solidity z=+30.5. That is why both the microscopist on e7 (density higher vs DMSO, candidates: Microtubule stabilizers) and I weighted stabilizers heavily.
- However the atlas comparison never supported a confident stabilizer call. e6 NSC vote was Protein degradation 1/4 with k-neighbours Microtubule destabilizers 6/10, Microtubule stabilizers 4/10. e17 on second comparison was NSC 1/4 Protein degradation with k-neighbours 5/10 stabilizers, 4/10 destabilizers, 1/10 Protein degradation. The review correctly called this a 4-way per-well split and a 5 vs 4 neighbour tie at similar similarity ~0.368. I had this signal but underweighted it.
- Low-dose morphology e4 (0.3uM, 63 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+15.3, act_std +14.9, nuc_major_axis +13.6) and e2 (1uM, 103 cells: cell_roundness -26.4, solidity -26.3, nuc_area_ratio +16.2) showed enlargement/elongation. High-dose e3 (30uM, 410 cells: nuc_solidity -414.8, act_tub_ratio -159.3, nuc_form_factor -133.9) was extreme, likely toxic/artifact. The dose-response calculations e8-e14 showed no significant monotonic tubulin trend: tub_mean rho -0.40 p=0.6, cell_roundness 0.00 p=1, tub_glcm_contrast -0.20 p=0.8, cell_count +0.40 p=0.6, nuc_area -0.80 p=0.2, act_tub_ratio -0.80 p=0.2. Only frac_large_nucleus e10 was borderline rho -0.95 p=0.051. In other words, there was no robust dose-response to anchor stabilizers vs destabilizers, and the single-well 3uM spike drove the call.
- lookup_compound e21/e22 confirmed identity MG-132, PubChem CID 462382, ChEMBL CHEMBL64925, with no curated mechanism, and name/BBBC021 structure agree. I incorrectly treated 'none curated' as absence of evidence for Protein degradation, rather than as uninformative. Literature search e23 returned 523 hits for MG-132 proteasome inhibitor / protein degradation and e24 returned 2 hits for proteasome inhibitor mimicking microtubule stabilization. I did not integrate this. PMID 24992982 explicitly describes MG-132 as a proteasome inhibitor, and PMID 11562742 and PMID 40450326 describe proteasome-mediated / proteasome-dependent degradation, consistent with the true Protein degradation MOA. I cited none of this in my hypothesis updates.

What misled me and why:
- Overweighting e5: I took tub_glcm_contrast +151.7 and tub_mean +54.7 in a single well with only 39 cells as definitive bundling/stabilization. With n=39, this should have flagged low sampling / selective survival rather than a class-specific phenotype. The abrupt reversal from e2 rounding -26.4 at 1uM to +30.5 at 3uM is biologically plausible as a toxicity-related shape change, not proof of stabilization, as the review noted.
- Overweighting e7 microscopist 'stabilizers' on 4 fields at higher density, and discounting e18 microscopist on 3 fields at lower density with candidates unknown and e3 extreme nuclear irregularity. I used the visual description of 'diffuse, intensely bright tubulin' as stabilizer-like, when it could equally fit depolymerization/diffuse accumulation or proteasome-inhibition-induced protein accumulation.
- Misreading the atlas: I listed Protein degradation 0.05 in step 15 and 0.08 in step 19 hypothesis_history despite it being the only NSC vote present in e6 and e17. I elevated Microtubule stabilizers to 0.62 then 0.48 based on e5+e7 while k-neighbours were essentially tied. This was over-calibrated given the per-well tie.
- Ignoring that proteasome inhibition is known to cause secondary cell-cycle/nuclear enlargement and cytoskeletal changes including apparent microtubule stabilization phenotypes - the 2 hits in e24. Without integrating that, the tubulin hyperintensity looked exclusively like a primary microtubule agent.

Acquisition choices:
- I used list_available_experiments e1 (8 doses 0.03-100uM, 4 of 4 wells) and acquired only single replicates at 0.3uM e4, 1uM e2, 3uM e5, 30uM e3, leaving 0 wells. This left the decisive 3uM signal unreplicated. The requested experiment was dose 4 replicate 2 at 3uM to replicate hyperintensity/contrast and rounding reversal. Budget exhaustion made verification impossible. Better would have been to sample fewer extreme doses or include replicates upfront for the key transition dose.
- I ran 7 dose_response tests but none were significant, which should have reduced confidence rather than being set aside in update_hypotheses e15/e19.

Lesson: With a tied atlas and a single low-n well driving the phenotype, retain Protein degradation as a leading hypothesis for MG-132-type proteasome inhibitors, especially when large-nucleus and extreme actin/tubulin ratio features are present, and require replicate confirmation before calling a primary cytoskeletal MOA based on tubulin intensity/texture alone.

e4 low-dose enlarged nucleus and e2 elongation flagged a non-primary tubulin cell-cycle effect that fits proteasome inhibition
Dose-response e8-e14 non-significant p values correctly indicated no robust tubulin dose trend
Lookup e21/e22 verified MG-132 identity and PubMed search e23/e24 returned proteasome and proteasome-microtubule literature that I should have weighted
what_was_wrong: Overweighted single-well e5 39-cell tub_mean +54.7 / tub_glcm_contrast +151.7 as definitive stabilizer bundling
Misapplied e7 microscopist stabilizer call while discounting e18 lower density unknown call and e3 artifactual extremes
Assigned Protein degradation 0.05-0.08 despite it being the only NSC class voted
Treated lack of curated ChEMBL mechanism as evidence against Protein degradation

Example of proteasome-mediated degradation phenotype relevant to Protein degradation class

Requested: acquire dose 4 (3uM) replicate 2 to replicate tubulin hyperintensity and rounding signal before distinguishing stabilizers vs destabilizers vs secondary proteasome effect; plus orthogonal proteasome activity and tubulin polymerization controls.

## Reflection

Unblinded truth: Protein degradation (MG-132). My final submitted call: Microtubule stabilizers p=0.48, previously p=0.62. Verdict: incorrect.

What the evidence got right:
- The quantitative image features were dominated by a strong tubulin signal at the intermediate dose. Well w_b7bdfca819 (dose 4, 3uM, rep1) in e5 showed tub_glcm_contrast z=+151.7 and tub_mean z=+54.7 with cell_solidity z=+30.5. That is why both the microscopist on e7 (density higher vs DMSO, candidates: Microtubule stabilizers) and I weighted stabilizers heavily.
- However the atlas comparison never supported a confident stabilizer call. e6 NSC vote was Protein degradation 1/4 with k-neighbours Microtubule destabilizers 6/10, Microtubule stabilizers 4/10. e17 on second comparison was NSC 1/4 Protein degradation with k-neighbours 5/10 stabilizers, 4/10 destabilizers, 1/10 Protein degradation. The review correctly called this a 4-way per-well split and a 5 vs 4 neighbour tie at similar similarity ~0.368. I had this signal but underweighted it.
- Low-dose morphology e4 (0.3uM, 63 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+15.3, act_std +14.9, nuc_major_axis +13.6) and e2 (1uM, 103 cells: cell_roundness -26.4, solidity -26.3, nuc_area_ratio +16.2) showed enlargement/elongation. High-dose e3 (30uM, 410 cells: nuc_solidity -414.8, act_tub_ratio -159.3, nuc_form_factor -133.9) was extreme, likely toxic/artifact. The dose-response calculations e8-e14 showed no significant monotonic tubulin trend: tub_mean rho -0.40 p=0.6, cell_roundness 0.00 p=1, tub_glcm_contrast -0.20 p=0.8, cell_count +0.40 p=0.6, nuc_area -0.80 p=0.2, act_tub_ratio -0.80 p=0.2. Only frac_large_nucleus e10 was borderline rho -0.95 p=0.051. In other words, there was no robust dose-response to anchor stabilizers vs destabilizers, and the single-well 3uM spike drove the call.
- lookup_compound e21/e22 confirmed identity MG-132, PubChem CID 462382, ChEMBL CHEMBL64925, with no curated mechanism, and name/BBBC021 structure agree. I incorrectly treated 'none curated' as absence of evidence for Protein degradation, rather than as uninformative. Literature search e23 returned 523 hits for MG-132 proteasome inhibitor / protein degradation and e24 returned 2 hits for proteasome inhibitor mimicking microtubule stabilization. I did not integrate this. PMID 24992982 explicitly describes MG-132 as a proteasome inhibitor, and PMID 11562742 and PMID 40450326 describe proteasome-mediated / proteasome-dependent degradation, consistent with the true Protein degradation MOA. I cited none of this in my hypothesis updates.

What misled me and why:
- Overweighting e5: I took tub_glcm_contrast +151.7 and tub_mean +54.7 in a single well with only 39 cells as definitive bundling/stabilization. With n=39, this should have flagged low sampling / selective survival rather than a class-specific phenotype. The abrupt reversal from e2 rounding -26.4 at 1uM to +30.5 at 3uM is biologically plausible as a toxicity-related shape change, not proof of stabilization, as the review noted.
- Overweighting e7 microscopist 'stabilizers' on 4 fields at higher density, and discounting e18 microscopist on 3 fields at lower density with candidates unknown and e3 extreme nuclear irregularity. I used the visual description of 'diffuse, intensely bright tubulin' as stabilizer-like, when it could equally fit depolymerization/diffuse accumulation or proteasome-inhibition-induced protein accumulation.
- Misreading the atlas: I listed Protein degradation 0.05 in step 15 and 0.08 in step 19 hypothesis_history despite it being the only NSC vote present in e6 and e17. I elevated Microtubule stabilizers to 0.62 then 0.48 based on e5+e7 while k-neighbours were essentially tied. This was over-calibrated given the per-well tie.
- Ignoring that proteasome inhibition is known to cause secondary cell-cycle/nuclear enlargement and cytoskeletal changes including apparent microtubule stabilization phenotypes - the 2 hits in e24. Without integrating that, the tubulin hyperintensity looked exclusively like a primary microtubule agent.

Acquisition choices:
- I used list_available_experiments e1 (8 doses 0.03-100uM, 4 of 4 wells) and acquired only single replicates at 0.3uM e4, 1uM e2, 3uM e5, 30uM e3, leaving 0 wells. This left the decisive 3uM signal unreplicated. The requested experiment was dose 4 replicate 2 at 3uM to replicate hyperintensity/contrast and rounding reversal. Budget exhaustion made verification impossible. Better would have been to sample fewer extreme doses or include replicates upfront for the key transition dose.
- I ran 7 dose_response tests but none were significant, which should have reduced confidence rather than being set aside in update_hypotheses e15/e19.

Lesson: With a tied atlas and a single low-n well driving the phenotype, retain Protein degradation as a leading hypothesis for MG-132-type proteasome inhibitors, especially when large-nucleus and extreme actin/tubulin ratio features are present, and require replicate confirmation before calling a primary cytoskeletal MOA based on tubulin intensity/texture alone.

What was right:
- Atlas NSC consistently retained Protein degradation 1/4 in e6 and e17 despite my low probability
- e4 low-dose enlarged nucleus and e2 elongation flagged a non-primary tubulin cell-cycle effect that fits proteasome inhibition
- Dose-response e8-e14 non-significant p values correctly indicated no robust tubulin dose trend
- Lookup e21/e22 verified MG-132 identity and PubMed search e23/e24 returned proteasome and proteasome-microtubule literature that I should have weighted

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted single-well e5 39-cell tub_mean +54.7 / tub_glcm_contrast +151.7 as definitive stabilizer bundling
- Misapplied e7 microscopist stabilizer call while discounting e18 lower density unknown call and e3 artifactual extremes
- Assigned Protein degradation 0.05-0.08 despite it being the only NSC class voted
- Treated lack of curated ChEMBL mechanism as evidence against Protein degradation

Proposed next experiment: Rejected in review due to tie and single-well reliance.
